    "content": "<p>So, you have multiple projects and one or more of them have dependencies (or\njust plain don't work) on certain versions of node? What to do?\n<a href=\"https://github.com/creationix/nvm\">Node Version Manager (NVM) allows you to install and switch between them &quot;with ease&quot;</a>\n(quotes added as I'm writing this blog post as I get it installed for the first\ntime myself... lets see just how easy it is!).</p>\n<!--more-->\n<h2>Before You Install - Uninstall Node!</h2>\n<p>Although it's optional to remove previous node installations, it's recommended.\nThere's a\n<a href=\"https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11177954/how-do-i-completely-uninstall-node-js-and-reinstall-from-beginning-mac-os-x\">great post on Stack Overflow that describes how to remove nodejs manually and for this that used brew to originally install node</a>.</p>\n<h2>Ensure you have the Xcode command line tools.</h2>\n<p>The Xcode command line tools (which you may already have for other reasons) are\nrequired. The easiest way to install them is to run the following in the\nterminal:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">xcode-select --install\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Run the NVM Install Script</h2>\n<p>You can either use cURL or Wget to install NVM. To test if you have either, just\ntype curl or wget into a terminal window and hit return. If you get some kind of\nresponse that isn't an error, you know which to use. Otherwise, you can install\nwget via brew:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">brew install wget\n</code></pre>\n<p>Then you'll want to run the latest install script mentioned on the\n<a href=\"https://github.com/creationix/nvm\">NVM repo</a>. <strong>Go there and copy+paste into\nyour terminal window</strong>.</p>\n<p>After it installs, you ought to be able to open a fresh terminal window and type\nin <strong>nvm</strong> and see some kind of output, but not this:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">$ nvm\n-bash: nvm: command not found\n</code></pre>\n<p>If you got that, it means that your shell isn't configured to use nvm. What I\nfound after investigating is that NVM had added references to itself to the\n.bashrc file directly in my home directory. You can see this by typing the\nfollowing in a terminal:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">open $HOME/.bashrc\n</code></pre>\n<p>However, it hadn't added itself to the .bash_profile file.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">open $HOME/.bash_profile\n</code></pre>\n<p>A kind user on Stack Exchange explains that\n<a href=\"https://apple.stackexchange.com/questions/51036/what-is-the-difference-between-bash-profile-and-bashrc\">on OS X, every time terminal is run it considers it a <em>login terminal</em> which uses the .bash_profile file and not the .bashrc file</a>.\nAn easy fix for this though is to just consolidate all of the customizations to\nthe terminal load process into the .bashrc file.</p>\n<p>Add the following to your .bash_profile and move its contents into .bashrc.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">if [ -f $HOME/.bashrc ]; then\n        source $HOME/.bashrc\nfi\n</code></pre>\n<p>Fire up a fresh terminal and run the following, which should output <strong>nvm</strong> if\nthe install was successful.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">command -v nvm\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Install Node Versions</h2>\n<p>We've got NVM, now let's install the versions of node we want to use across\nourprojects.</p>\n<h4>Latest node</h4>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">nvm install node\n</code></pre>\n<h4>Specific version of Node</h4>\n<p><a href=\"https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/dev/spfx/set-up-your-development-environment\">Version 6.11.5 of node.js is required for SharePoint Framework development</a>\nas of this writing.</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">nvm install 6.11.5\n</code></pre>\n<p>Note that you can list all available installed node versions using the following\ncommandline:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">nvm ls\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Configure your project to use a specific version</h2>\n<p>For this, we're going to place a .nvmrc into the root of each project that\nutilizes node which indicates which version to use.</p>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p>Get to the target directory</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Run one of the following:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">echo &quot;5.9&quot; &gt; .nvmrc\n\necho &quot;lts/*&quot; &gt; .nvmrc # to default to the latest LTS version\n\necho &quot;node&quot; &gt; .nvmrc # to default to the latest version\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Start using that node version using the following command:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-shell\">nvm use\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>(optional) You can configure auto-switching to the desired node version\ninstead of having to type nvm use. This requires using\n<a href=\"https://github.com/wbyoung/avn\">AVN (Automatic Version Switching for Node)</a>\nwhich works in conjunction with the .nvmrc file.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n",

        "rawInput": "\nSo, you have multiple projects and one or more of them have dependencies (or\njust plain don't work) on certain versions of node? What to do?\n[Node Version Manager (NVM) allows you to install and switch between them \"with ease\"](https://github.com/creationix/nvm)\n(quotes added as I'm writing this blog post as I get it installed for the first\ntime myself... lets see just how easy it is!).\n\n<!--more-->\n\n## Before You Install - Uninstall Node!\n\nAlthough it's optional to remove previous node installations, it's recommended.\nThere's a\n[great post on Stack Overflow that describes how to remove nodejs manually and for this that used brew to originally install node](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11177954/how-do-i-completely-uninstall-node-js-and-reinstall-from-beginning-mac-os-x).\n\n## Ensure you have the Xcode command line tools.\n\nThe Xcode command line tools (which you may already have for other reasons) are\nrequired. The easiest way to install them is to run the following in the\nterminal:\n\n```shell\nxcode-select --install\n```\n\n## Run the NVM Install Script\n\nYou can either use cURL or Wget to install NVM. To test if you have either, just\ntype curl or wget into a terminal window and hit return. If you get some kind of\nresponse that isn't an error, you know which to use. Otherwise, you can install\nwget via brew:\n\n```shell\nbrew install wget\n```\n\nThen you'll want to run the latest install script mentioned on the\n[NVM repo](https://github.com/creationix/nvm). **Go there and copy+paste into\nyour terminal window**.\n\nAfter it installs, you ought to be able to open a fresh terminal window and type\nin **nvm** and see some kind of output, but not this:\n\n```shell\n$ nvm\n-bash: nvm: command not found\n```\n\nIf you got that, it means that your shell isn't configured to use nvm. What I\nfound after investigating is that NVM had added references to itself to the\n.bashrc file directly in my home directory. You can see this by typing the\nfollowing in a terminal:\n\n```shell\nopen $HOME/.bashrc\n```\n\nHowever, it hadn't added itself to the .bash_profile file.\n\n```shell\nopen $HOME/.bash_profile\n```\n\nA kind user on Stack Exchange explains that\n[on OS X, every time terminal is run it considers it a _login terminal_ which uses the .bash_profile file and not the .bashrc file](https://apple.stackexchange.com/questions/51036/what-is-the-difference-between-bash-profile-and-bashrc).\nAn easy fix for this though is to just consolidate all of the customizations to\nthe terminal load process into the .bashrc file.\n\nAdd the following to your .bash_profile and move its contents into .bashrc.\n\n```shell\nif [ -f $HOME/.bashrc ]; then\n        source $HOME/.bashrc\nfi\n```\n\nFire up a fresh terminal and run the following, which should output **nvm** if\nthe install was successful.\n\n```shell\ncommand -v nvm\n```\n\n## Install Node Versions\n\nWe've got NVM, now let's install the versions of node we want to use across\nourprojects.\n\n#### Latest node\n\n```shell\nnvm install node\n```\n\n#### Specific version of Node\n\n[Version 6.11.5 of node.js is required for SharePoint Framework development](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/dev/spfx/set-up-your-development-environment)\nas of this writing.\n\n```shell\nnvm install 6.11.5\n```\n\nNote that you can list all available installed node versions using the following\ncommandline:\n\n```shell\nnvm ls\n```\n\n## Configure your project to use a specific version\n\nFor this, we're going to place a .nvmrc into the root of each project that\nutilizes node which indicates which version to use.\n\n1. Get to the target directory\n2. Run one of the following:\n\n    ```shell\n    echo \"5.9\" > .nvmrc\n\n    echo \"lts/*\" > .nvmrc # to default to the latest LTS version\n\n    echo \"node\" > .nvmrc # to default to the latest version\n    ```\n\n3. Start using that node version using the following command:\n\n    ```shell\n    nvm use\n    ```\n\n4. (optional) You can configure auto-switching to the desired node version\n   instead of having to type nvm use. This requires using\n   [AVN (Automatic Version Switching for Node)](https://github.com/wbyoung/avn)\n   which works in conjunction with the .nvmrc file.\n",
